distractors.reason: 'Look for' means searching for something you lost or need (look for my keys). It does not mean observing a picture.
'Look after' means taking care of a person or thing (look after a baby). We don't use it to mean observing a picture.
'Look in' means checking inside something (look in the box). It does not mean observing a picture on a page.

example_sentence: Please look ___ the picture on page five.
l1_interference: Los hispanohablantes suelen omitir la preposición porque en español el verbo 'mirar' se usa directamente con el complemento: 'mirar la foto'. Por eso a veces dicen 'look the picture' en lugar de 'look at the picture'.
explanation: In English, 'look' needs the preposition 'at' to show the direction of your eyes toward something: look at the picture, look at the board.

related_collocations.example: Please listen to the teacher carefully.
I am waiting for the bus.
I am looking for my keys.

memory_tip: LOOK AT = point your eyes at something (look at the picture) | LOOK FOR = search for something (look for the keys)
